people: Sui Grand Preceptor and Duke of Shen
Grandson and heir of Li Mu
Commander of the crown prince Left Guard
Widow of Emperor Xuan of Zhou

claims.event: Rescued the Zhou founder at Mangshan by lashing him as a common soldier, refused Yuchi Jiong, and urged Yang Jian to take the throne and move the capital.
Claimed ancestor of Li Mu who died in Xiongnu captivity.
Served as area commander at Gaoping and settled the family there.
Died early and was posthumously made Minister of Works when Li Mu rose.
Thrown from his horse at Mangshan and saved by Li Mu, whom he rewarded with all the piebald horses in his stables.
Escorted to power by Li Mu near the end of Yongxi.
Took Jiangling with Li Mu.
Granted rank equal to the Three Excellencies after his father victory over the Qu and Mian tribes.
Counted among the founding ministers of Zhou.
A founding minister executed under Yuwen Hu after ignoring Li Mu warnings about his son Zhi.
Received the marquisate of Shengqian that Li Mu ceded to him.
Executed Li Yuan and Li Zhi but spared Li Mu and Li Ji.
Executed with his father under Yuwen Hu regency.
Marked for death but spared after Li Mu offered two sons in his place.
Received Li Mu gold belt and memorial urging him to take the throne; made him Grand Preceptor.
Sent envoys to win Li Mu to his rebellion; Mu detained them.
Secretly urged his father to rebel with the Bingzhou troops.
Cited by the Sui emperor as aiding Zhou at a hundred years.
Cited by the Sui emperor as serving Han in great old age.
Granted immunity from prosecution short of treason; died at home in Kaihuang 6 aged seventy-seven.
Rose under Zhou to Duke of Anle and governor of Fengzhou, dying before his father.
Carried Li Mu iron to Yang Jian, had his nephew Yun murdered, and bribed Yuwen Shu to win the Duke of Shen title.
Moved the capital on Li Mu memorial and detained the whole clan after Li Yun murder.
Urged moving the capital, and later asked that Li Yun fief be extinguished for kin-slaying.
Cited in the edict praising Li Mu as free of his failings.
Cited in the edict praising Li Mu.
Sent with the lamentation text for Li Mu funeral.
Inherited the title in Kaihuang 8 and was murdered at the instigation of his uncle Hun.
Sent by Li Hun to murder Li Yun and escaped punishment.
Falsely accused by Li Hun of the murder and executed.
Rose to rank equal to the Three Excellencies and was posthumously made governor of Weizhou.
Captured by Chen in Jiangxi, later routed Tuyuhun by a feigned truce on the Tao River.
Led the failed Jiangxi campaign on which Li Ya was captured.
Became governor of Yanzhou and Marquis of Yangqu.
Became governor of Hezhou and Duke of Changcheng.
Became General of Chariots and Cavalry and Marquis of Guizheng.
Rose to Pillar of the State and Duke of Mi.
Rebelled at Ye; Yang Jian feared he would win over Li Mu.
Received Li Hun conveying Li Mu intent.
Took Li Hun with him to Yangzhou as head of his trusted guard.
Led the campaign on which Li Hun defeated the Turks at the Nayuan River.
Defeated by Li Hun on the Nayuan River.
Bribed by Li Hun, his brother-in-law, to recommend him as heir of Li Mu.

label.en: Commissioner Equal to the Three Excellencies
Senior Equal to the Three Excellencies
General of the Left Martial Guard
General of the Right Valiant Guard
Grand General of the Right Valiant Guard
Commander of the Crown Prince Left Guard

claims.event: Stopped paying Yuwen Shu, who then framed him with the Li prophecy; executed with thirty-two kinsmen.
Set counter-fires to keep Prince Zhi of Wei rebels out, and urged supervision of the army against Yuchi Jiong.
Wept on being made a marquis as a boy, and abandoned Yuchi Jiong after Li Mu sided with Yang Jian.
Framed Li Hun with the Li prophecy and dictated a false memorial to Li Min wife.
Heard drunk Yuwen Shu vow never to forget Li Hun betrayal.
Told the emperor during the Liaodong campaign that a Li would become Son of Heaven.
Accused with Li Hun of plotting treason and executed.
Named by Yuwen Shu as meeting secretly with Li Hun.
Sent by Yuwen Shu to accuse Li Hun of treason.
Jointly interrogated Li Hun and found no proof of rebellion.
Jointly interrogated Li Hun and found no proof of rebellion.
Coerced by Yuwen Shu into writing a secret memorial accusing the Li family.
Rose to Supreme Pillar for pacifying the southern tribes early in Kaihuang.
Father of Li Xun and Li Chong, who marveled at Chong tears on being made a marquis.
Visited Yunyang Palace and conquered Qi, drawing Li Chong into his councils.
Rebelled and burned the Sushang Gate.
As chancellor sent Wei Xiaokuan against Yuchi Jiong.
Rebelled and sent envoys to win over Li Chong.
Led the army against Yuchi Jiong and kept Li Chong under watch.
Sent to supervise the army at Li Xun request.
Succeeded to Li Xun title.
Led the campaign against Qi in which Li Chong excelled.
Pledged Bingzhou to Yang Jian, which turned Li Chong from Yuchi Jiong.
Defeated, after which Li Chong was made Grand General.

claims.event: Held the ruined Sand Fort against the Turks, refused their offer to become a tegin, and died charging them at forty-eight.
Won Princess Leping daughter in marriage and, by refusing lesser ranks, was made Pillar of the State; executed with the Li Hun clan at thirty-nine.
Raised in the Zhou palace with the founder sons, he repelled Qi raiders at Xinan and fought Hulu Mingyue at Luoyang.
Raised Li Min in the palace and, delighted by his singing, made him Pillar of the State.
His widow became Princess Leping.
Chose Li Min as husband for her daughter and on her deathbed asked that her fief income go to him.
Married Li Min after her mother auditioned noble youths at Hongsheng Palace.
Granted Li Min Princess Leping fief, then suspected his name Hong of fulfilling a prophecy.
His revolt preceded Li Min plan for the new capital at Daxing.
Met secretly with Li Min and was executed with him.
Met privately with Li Min.
Reported Li Min secret meetings to the emperor.
Given poison wine several months after Li Min execution.
Father of Liang Rui, served Western Wei as Grand Commandant.
Raised Liang Rui in the palace with his own sons.
Granted Liang Rui an open office and the dukedom of Wulong.
On taking the throne recalled Liang Rui as Imperial Bearer.
Led Liang Rui against Hulu Mingyue at Luoyang.
Opposed Prince Xian and Liang Rui at Luoyang.
Under him Liang Rui governed Fu and commanded Liang and An.

label.en: Acting General of the Garrison Guard

claims.event: Crushed Wang Qian rebellion in Shu, executed him at Chengdu, and memorialized for the conquest of Nanning.
Appointed Liang Rui campaign commander-in-chief against Wang Qian.
Rebelled in Shu, was shut out of Chengdu by his own officers, captured by Wang Bao and executed by Liang Rui.
Served under Liang Rui and attacked Daxi Ji by a separate route.
Broke Li Sanwang at Tonggu Pass and attacked Daxi Ji.
Campaign commander under Liang Rui against Wang Qian.
Campaign commander under Liang Rui against Wang Qian.
Campaign commander under Liang Rui against Wang Qian.
Held Tonggu Pass for Wang Qian and was broken by Zhang Wei.
Massed a hundred thousand men in defile camps and was routed by Liang Rui night attack.
Held the defile camps with Zhao Yan and was routed by Liang Rui.
Surrendered Jiange to Liang Rui in fear.
Surrendered Pinglin to Liang Rui in fear.
Sent with Daxi Ji against Lizhou.
Seized Kaiyuan, was broken by Liang Rui, then surrendered Chengdu and shut out Wang Qian.
Sent by Liang Rui toward Jiange.
Grand General sent by Liang Rui toward Baxi.
Grand General who led a river fleet up the Jialing.
Attacked Daxi Ji by a separate route.
Attacked Daxi Ji by a separate route.
Attacked Daxi Ji by a separate route.
Attacked Daxi Ji by a separate route.
Held Chengdu with Daxi Ji and surrendered it, refusing Wang Qian entry.
Captured the fleeing Wang Qian.
Refused allegiance relying on remoteness and sent only a few dozen horses as tribute.
Summoned by Xiangdong to march on Jingzhou, leaving Nanning open.
Summoned Xu Wensheng to Jingzhou.
Seized Nanning and was confirmed as inspector from afar.
Former envoy to Nanning sent to court with Liang Rui memorial.
Approved but deferred Liang Rui Nanning and Chen plans, secretly fearing his prestige.
Sent to pacify Nanning following Liang Rui plan.
Urged the conquest of Nanning and Chen, had Xue Daheng urge Yang Jian to take the throne, and proposed frontier measures against the Turks.
Told Liang Rui at a banquet in Shu that the empire hope had turned to Sui.
Cited in the Sui edict as an enemy Guangwu treated as emperor.
Cited in the Sui edict as an enemy Guangwu treated as emperor.
Cited as making peace with Gongsun Shu and Wei Xiao.
Cited as at first refusing to submit to Gaozu of Han.
Cited as the ruler Zhao Tuo would not serve.
Cited for replying to Jin on plain white paper.
Cited as receiving Sun Hao reply.
Cited by Liang Rui as refusing a residence while the Xiongnu remained.
Cited by Liang Rui as offering himself for punishment while the Xianlian held out.
Took bribes after defeating Wang Qian to tarnish his own fame, retired pleading illness, and died at Luoyang aged sixty-five.
His defeat by Liang Rui led to inflated merit rolls and protests.
Succeeded Liang Rui and inherited the retroactive title Duke of Dai.
Judged by the historian as first raised to Grand Tutor, yet shamed beside Wang Ling, his descendants destroyed.
Entrusted Li Mu and Liang Rui with his deepest confidence as his enterprise began.
Cited by the historian as a model of loyalty before whom Li Mu and Liang Rui must feel shame.
Cited by the historian as a loyal Jin minister shaming Li Mu and Liang Rui.
